transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Torres (Redwood AE), Chris Li (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Aurora Head of AI), Samir Khan (Aurora Cloud Architect), Lena Ortiz (Aurora Security)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jamie, AE on the Redwood side, with Chris our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: good, thanks. short on time so we want to focus on private networking, residency, and what success looks like for a POC.
[00:15] Chris: great, we'll aim to keep it focused. quick agenda: networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), regions and residency, egress and billing, workload sizing for benchmarks, and then success criteria & timeline. sound ok?
[00:28] Samir: yes, that's perfect. we want something that doesn't force traffic over the public internet and ensures data stays in our regions.
[00:35] Lena: also need to confirm KMS integration and audit logs for any private deployment.
[00:40] Jamie: totally. quick question on scope — is this POC intended to run in our VPC or are you looking for Redwood Private deployed into your environment?
[00:50] Maya: preference is Redwood Private via VPC peering or PrivateLink. we want the control plane out of band but the inference traffic must stay in our VPC, and all logs/data must be resident in us-east-2 for PHI compliance.
[01:05] Chris: understood. just to note, PrivateLink tends to be easier for cross-account controlled ingress, while VPC peering gives lower latency but requires route table config and peering approvals. both are supported.
[01:20] Samir: latency is important — our target p95 for chat responses is below 450ms when serving a 512-token context, and baseline QPS is about 20 concurrent sessions with bursts to 60.
[01:33] Chris: OK that's helpful. for sizing we'll model GPUs and batching to meet that SLO. two approaches for POC: use Redwood Dedicated in your cloud account with peering, or Redwood Private where we install a Private control plane and inference nodes in your VPC.
[01:50] Maya: can you clarify the differences on egress billing? we can't have data leaving the region, and egress costs balloon if traffic crosses AZs or out to public.
[01:59] Jamie: good point — with peering or PrivateLink, traffic stays in-region so normal intra-region transfer rules apply. if you route to a hosted region we don't recommend that for PHI. we'll include egress notes in the pricing doc.
[02:12] Lena: about KMS — we need customer-managed keys, rotation policy, and proof that Redwood won't cache keys.
[02:20] Chris: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations; keys remain in your KMS and we use envelope encryption. we'll add a short diagram. FYI the auto transcript might say 'envelope' oddly as 'in vault' sometimes.
[02:34] [minor crosstalk]
[02:40] Samir: on networking, do you support AWS PrivateLink endpoints? we use service consumer/provider mode.
[02:46] Chris: yes, PrivateLink is supported for the API endpoint. we can publish endpoint service and you create the interface endpoint in your VPC. alternatively, VPC peering is supported for a more direct route — depends on security team preference.
[02:58] Maya: which one is faster?
[03:00] Chris: usually peering has slightly lower latency; PrivateLink adds a small hop but isolates the control plane. for tight SLOs peering + placement in the same AZs works best, but requires routing coordination.
[03:12] Samir: ok. for the POC we can try PrivateLink first to get approvals quicker, then test peering if latency isn't good enough.
[03:20] Jamie: sounds pragmatic. for benchmarks we'll run three scenarios: 1) latency p50/p90/p95 for 512-token contexts single-user; 2) throughput with 20 concurrent sessions steady state and 60 burst; 3) quality/regression checks using your 200 prompt eval set. does that cover it?
[03:38] Maya: yes. also include cold-start token timings and KV cache behavior — we want to see caching benefits.
[03:45] Chris: we'll capture both cold and warm starts. note: some transcript text might show 'K V cache' spaced — that's our KV cache.
[03:52] Lena: audit logs — need to know retention, what fields are logged, and whether we can ship logs to our SIEM.
[03:59] Jamie: Redwood can forward audit logs to your S3 or CloudWatch and you can glue them into Splunk/Datadog. retention config is per-account; we'll include default options and longer retention add-ons.
[04:12] Samir: network prep — what information do you need from our side to set up PrivateLink?
[04:18] Chris: we'll need a list of subnets and security groups for the interface endpoints, the AWS account ID for endpoint creation, and IP ranges if you prefer NACLs. for peering we'll need VPC IDs and route table owners.
[04:31] Maya: timeline?
[04:33] Jamie: propose 4-week POC: week 0 prep (networking and infra access), week 1 deploy & smoke tests, week 2 run benchmarks, week 3 analyze results and iterate, decision at end of week 4. can shorten if Aurora provides quick approvals.
[04:48] Maya: that works if we can get networking approvals in 3 business days.
[04:52] Lena: our security checklist will need SOC2 evidence and a short runbook for incident response.
[04:58] Jamie: we'll attach SOC2 report and an incident response playbook excerpt.
[05:02] [pause / typing sounds]
[05:10] Samir: on model variants — do you support quantized variants to reduce GPU footprint? we want to trade off latency vs cost.
[05:18] Chris: yes — we support quantized runtimes and can recommend kernel profiles. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching settings per workload. for the POC we'll include a small param sweep for cost vs latency.
[05:31] Maya: for success criteria, our stakeholders want: (1) <450ms p95 for 512 tokens, (2) cost-per-request below $0.015 at expected QPS, (3) network traffic never leaves us-east-2, (4) KMS CMK integration and audit log forwarding. if we hit those we go to pilot.
[05:51] Jamie: clear. we'll map each criterion to bench steps and an acceptance signoff.
[05:56] Chris: on benchmarking methodology we'll provide a script (JMeter / k6) and an instrumentation dashboard — we'll pre-install tracing hooks so you can see per-token latency and batching stats.
[06:10] Maya: perfect. minor note — our compliance team will want a short privacy/dataflow diagram.
[06:16] Jamie: will include that with the networking diagrams.
[06:20] Samir: can you share a sample Terraform snippet for PrivateLink / endpoint creation?
[06:25] Chris: yes, will share a snippet and a diagram; sometimes the snippet references 'aws_vpc_endpoint' which people copy incorrectly, we'll show the right parameters.
[06:34] Lena: are there any IP ranges we should expect to whitelist?
[06:38] Jamie: for PrivateLink you don't typically whitelist IPs — you create the interface endpoint in your VPC. for peering you'll need the Redwood subnet ranges; we can provide a minimal set.
[06:48] Maya: any gotchas about AZ placement?
[06:50] Chris: ensure the endpoint subnets span the AZs you want traffic in. for peering, route tables must have the right propagation; sometimes network teams forget to update security groups on the interface endpoints.
[07:02] Samir: ok noted.
[07:05] [small discussion about internal stakeholders and procurement timelines, short laughter]
[07:20] Jamie: procurement — any procurement/legal items to surface now?
[07:24] Maya: we have a standard BA A and DPA to attach; procurement will want SLAs and liability limits.
[07:29] Jamie: we'll surface standard SLAs for Dedicated/Private and revise if needed for enterprise.
[07:33] Lena: also need to confirm support for SSO (SAML) and RBAC audit trails.
[07:39] Chris: supported; we'll link RBAC docs.
[07:42] Maya: good.
[07:45] Jamie: ok let's recap next steps...
[07:48] [Recap begins]
[07:50] Jamie: action items — I'll send pricing for Dedicated and Private, Chris will send network diagrams and Terraform snippets, Lena will send security doc list, Maya will share expected QPS/concurrency and eval prompts. target dates in the action item list.
[08:05] Maya: thanks, appreciate the clarity. one more question: can you run the benchmark in eu-west-1 too? some of our European data sets must be tested in-region.
[08:15] Chris: yes we can spin up staging in eu-west-1 as well. note that model weights may be pulled from a central repo initially — we'll ensure everything is pulled into the region before tests to avoid cross-region egress.
[08:30] Samir: that cross-region pull could add a one-time heavy egress if not staged — make sure you pre-seed images.
[08:36] Chris: agreed, we'll pre-pull and snapshot images.
[08:40] Jamie: alright, if nothing else we'll adjourn. thanks everyone.
[08:44] Maya: thanks all.
